final_text:
**Claim 511492 has a low denial risk, and the tools don't support any one denial reason code.**

**Score:** The model gives a 3.2% probability of denial. The validation-set average is 18.1%, so this claim is about 15 points below average. It is a carrier claim for HCPCS 99408 (a substance-use screening and brief intervention service) with principal diagnosis Z73.3.

**Why it's low:** The HCPCS code 99408 is the main driver. It cuts the odds of denial by about 71%. The billing NPI, the place of service (11, office) and the diagnosis each lower the odds slightly. The tax number raises them slightly (+21%). No risk-rule signal stands out.

**Most plausible code:** If I had to pick one, it would be CARC 11 (the diagnosis doesn't support the procedure billed). A stress diagnosis paired with an alcohol or substance screening code could look mismatched. That is my inference. The model doesn't predict codes, and the SHAP output doesn't show a mismatch signal. The policy search found nothing on 99408. Codes 16 and 197 have no supporting evidence here either.

**Caveat:** The denial label in this project is synthetic. It was built from risk rules, so the score reflects that constructed label and not a real payer decision.
